verses.text: Around that time, Jesus and his disciples walked through grainfields on the Sabbath. The disciples were hungry, so they picked heads of grain and ate.
The Pharisees saw it and called Jesus out: “Look, your disciples are doing something the Law doesn’t allow on the Sabbath.”
He answered, “Haven’t you read what David did when he and his crew were hungry?”
“He went into God’s house and ate the sacred bread—which wasn’t lawful for him or his companions to eat, only for the priests.”
“Or haven’t you read in the Law that priests working in the temple on the Sabbath break the Sabbath rules, yet aren’t guilty?”
“I’m telling you, someone greater than the temple is here.”
“If you understood what this means—‘I want mercy, not sacrifice’—you wouldn’t have condemned people who aren’t guilty.”
“The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
Jesus left there and went into their synagogue.
A man with a disabled hand was there. They asked Jesus, “Is healing on the Sabbath allowed?”—hoping to accuse him.
He replied, “If one of you had a sheep that fell into a pit on the Sabbath, wouldn’t you grab it and pull it out?”
“A person is worth so much more than a sheep! So, yes—it’s right to do good on the Sabbath.”
Then he told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” The man stretched it out, and it was completely restored, just like the other one.
But the Pharisees left and plotted how they could destroy Jesus.
Jesus knew what they were planning, so he withdrew. Huge crowds followed him, and he healed them all.
He warned them not to make him known.
This fulfilled what Isaiah the prophet had spoken:
“Here is my servant, whom I chose—my beloved, the one who pleases me. I’ll put my Spirit on him, and he’ll announce justice to the nations.”
“He won’t fight or shout; no one will hear his voice out on the streets.”
“He won’t snap a bruised reed or snuff out a smoking wick, until he brings justice through to victory.”
“The nations will put their hope in his name.”
Then people brought him a man who was demon-possessed, blind, and unable to speak. Jesus healed him, and the man could both speak and see.
The whole crowd was amazed and asked, “Could this be David’s son?”
The Pharisees heard and said, “This man drives out demons only by Beelzebul, the ruler of demons.”
Jesus knew what they were thinking and told them, “A kingdom fighting itself is headed for ruin. A city or household split down the middle won’t stand.”
“If Satan drives Satan out, he’s fighting himself. How could his kingdom last?”
“If I drive out demons by Beelzebul, who gives your own people power to drive them out? They’ll be your judges.”
“But if I drive out demons by God’s Spirit, then God’s Kingdom has already come upon you.”
“How can someone break into a strong man’s house and take his stuff without first tying him up? Then the house can be robbed.”
“Whoever isn’t with me is against me; whoever doesn’t gather with me scatters.”
“So I’m telling you: every sin and insult against God can be forgiven, but speaking against the Spirit won’t be forgiven.”
“A word against the Son of Man can be forgiven. But speaking against the Holy Spirit won’t be forgiven—not in this age or the age to come.”
“Make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad. You know a tree by its fruit.”
“You snake brood! How can you, being evil, say anything good? The mouth speaks from whatever fills the heart.”
“A good person brings good things out of a good store inside; an evil person brings evil things out of an evil store.”
“I’m telling you, people will have to answer on judgment day for every careless word they speak.”
“Your own words will show you’re in the right—or condemn you.”
Then some teachers of the Law and Pharisees answered him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”
He answered, “An evil, unfaithful generation keeps asking for a sign. The only sign it’ll get is the sign of Jonah the prophet.”
“Just as Jonah spent three days and three nights inside the huge fish, the Son of Man will spend three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.”
“The people of Nineveh will stand up at judgment with this generation and condemn it. They turned back at Jonah’s preaching—and look, someone greater than Jonah is here.”
“The Queen of the South will rise at judgment with this generation and condemn it. She came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom—and look, someone greater than Solomon is here.”
“When an unclean spirit leaves someone, it travels through dry places looking for rest but doesn’t find any.”
“Then it says, ‘I’ll go back to the home I left.’ It returns and finds the place empty, swept clean, and put in order.”
“So it goes and brings along seven spirits worse than itself. They move in and settle there, and that person ends up worse than before. That’s how it’ll be with this evil generation.”
While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and brothers stood outside, hoping to talk with him.
Someone told him, “Your mother and brothers are outside, trying to speak with you.”
He answered the person, “Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?”
He pointed toward his disciples and said, “Look—here are my mother and my brothers!”
“Anyone who does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother, sister, and mother.”
